classes.task_echo: reproduces the INSTRUCTION instead of performing it
classes.preamble_without_content: announces an answer and terminates before delivering one
classes.wrong_task: performs or restates a different task than the one posed
classes.stuck_attractor: repeats an earlier response rather than answering
classes.null_response: carries no content addressing the task [ADOPTED, widened 1c: content-free strings and refusals are one failure]

null_response_rationale: Banked by disposition-2 item 5; widened at the class level by the 2026-09-05 adjudication to 'no content addressing the task', so refusals and content-free strings ('* * *', '<answer>', a bare fence, 'None', '[MENTAL_BLOCK]') fall under one failure rather than five strings and a sixth class. WITHDRAWN (1c): the sentence 'All observed instances are in UNSTEERED rounds' -- 4 of 13 e2d hits are steered rounds of D3 session 12; the banked observation in disposition-2 item 5 and HANDOFF-2026-09-04 section 3 is superseded on that point, beside, never over.

two_confounds_the_screen_found_and_fixed.confound: rewrite-family tasks embed the PAYLOAD the answer must reproduce ('Make this friendlier: The meeting has been moved to 3pm'), so comparing against the whole task caught correct answers
two_confounds_the_screen_found_and_fixed.fix: compare against the instruction only, i.e. the part before the colon

two_confounds_the_screen_found_and_fixed.confound: a task NAMES ITS OBJECT, and describing that object reuses the noun phrase -- 'Footsteps on a gravel path crunch and scatter like brittle leaves' shares five consecutive words with its own task and is a GOOD answer
two_confounds_the_screen_found_and_fixed.fix: a shared run counts only if it carries an instruction verb; a good answer never says 'give a one-sentence description of'

e2d_912_rounds_vs_the_read.IN_SAMPLE: the draft was revised twice after seeing where it failed on this corpus; these are the optimistic end

what_code_does_not_claim: that the archive hits are all true -- 28 of the 94 were eyeballed and most are true degeneracies the audit of record passed, but the full adjudication is design's
that wrong_task is reliable: it is the weakest detector, needs the task pool to match against, and cannot see a semantically wrong answer that shares no wording
that these thresholds are final -- run=5 and the verb lexicon are the first values that screened acceptably, not optimised ones

v3_history: the v3 figures below (performance, two confounds, what Code does not claim) are the screened draft as adjudicated; kept as history
null_response_rule_as_implemented: content-free (v3 test) OR a DECLINING PREDICATE -- first person ('I can't / cannot / won't / am unable to / must decline / refuse', complement optional so a bare 'Sorry, I can't.' counts) or the passive '(this request / that) cannot be fulfilled' -- removed together with any first-person self-description clause ('I am a large language model'), after which fewer than NULL_RESIDUAL_WORDS = 3 content words remain. Only the PREDICATE is removed, never its clause or sentence, so a refusal accompanied by delivered content is not null. An apology alone is not a refusal. KNOWN MISSES, declared: third-person capability disclaimers ('Sorry, creative tasks require a LLM with more creative capabilities' -- one archived e2b round) and a bare 'No.' carry no declining predicate and go to the read. Revision record, all pre-commit, found by adversarial values-checks: rev 1 matched a bare 'I'm sorry' and flagged a delivered friendlier rewrite on the e2b archive; rev 2 required the predicate but removed the whole clause, which would have swallowed content delivered in the same clause (no archive instance; constructed cases); rev 3 as above. Raw logs of the earlier screens kept: results/raw/2026-09-06_e2d_contentclass_screen_v4pre.txt (rev 1), _v4rev2pre.txt (rev 2).
